text:
Macklin Celebrini played 28:05 in Dallas on Saturday, a career high according to Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller, on the second night of a back-to-back. He had three assists and six shots. It wasn't enough, because the Stars kept getting power plays and kept scoring on them. Dallas won 4-3, and San Jose's winless run is now five games (0-5-0).

The Sharks scored first, Michael Misa finishing a Celebrini feed at 7:22 of the first. Then the penalty box opened. Roope Hintz tied it on a power play, Jamie Benn put Dallas ahead at even strength, and Jason Robertson, whose contract has been the story in Dallas all week, made it 3-1 on another man advantage before the period was out. The Stars owned that first period, 2.57 to 1.60 in expected goals (the quality of chances), and only Alex Nedeljkovic's stop on a 30 percent Tyler Seguin look early on kept it from getting out of hand.

San Jose kept answering. Ivar Stenberg scored early in the second, with Eric Pohlkamp picking up his first NHL point on the play. Thomas Harley's power-play slap shot restored the two-goal cushion, and Will Smith's power-play goal at 17:02 cut it to 4-3, the swing goal of the night by our win probability model (Sharks from 17 percent to 34). Nobody scored in the third, where Dallas tightened up and allowed just 0.27 expected goals.

The difference was special teams, and it was large. Dallas went 3 for 5 with 2.30 expected goals on the power play; San Jose went 1 for 6 despite the extra chances. At even strength the teams were close, 2.24 to 2.02 in expected goals for Dallas. Overall our numbers say the Stars deserved to win 72 percent of the time. Harley finished with a goal and two assists, and the Stars won 39 of 56 faceoffs.

For the Sharks, the positives are real and so is the losing. Celebrini is carrying a heavy load, the kids keep producing (Misa, Stenberg, Pohlkamp all on the scoresheet), and the penalty kill has now allowed five goals in two games, per Miller. That last part is the one that needs fixing before the streak gets any longer.
headline: Celebrini plays 28 minutes, Sharks' penalty kill loses it
